findings.description: AWS access key ID and secret access key are embedded in plain text in the instance user_data script. User data is readable by anyone with ec2:DescribeInstances or from the instance metadata service, leaking long-lived static credentials.
No metadata_options block sets http_tokens = "required", so the legacy unauthenticated IMDSv1 remains enabled and an SSRF in the web application can be used to steal instance credentials.
The instance does not specify root_block_device with encrypted = true, so the root EBS volume may be stored unencrypted.

The instance is launched in a subnet with map_public_ip_on_launch enabled and a route to an internet gateway, giving it a public IP and direct internet exposure rather than placing it in a private network layer.
Ingress rule allows TCP port 22 from 0.0.0.0/0, exposing SSH administration to the entire internet and enabling brute-force and exploit attempts.
Egress rule allows all protocols and ports to 0.0.0.0/0, providing an unrestricted data exfiltration and command-and-control channel.
Port 80 is open to 0.0.0.0/0, serving traffic in cleartext with no TLS, so data in transit is not protected.
The EBS volume does not set encrypted = true, so data written to the attached volume is stored unencrypted.
The snapshot is taken from an unencrypted volume and no encryption/KMS key is configured, so a copy of the data persists unencrypted and can be shared broadly.
The VPC flow log destination bucket has no server-side encryption configuration, so sensitive network audit logs are stored unencrypted.
No public access block, bucket policy, or ACL restriction is configured for the flow log bucket, leaving it open to accidental public or cross-account exposure of network logs.
The log bucket lacks versioning and access logging, so tampering with or deletion of flow log evidence would be undetectable and unrecoverable.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, placing workloads directly on the internet instead of in a private layer.
map_public_ip_on_launch = true causes every instance in this subnet to receive a public IP address, exposing workloads directly to the internet.
The VPC's default security group is not explicitly restricted with an aws_default_security_group resource, so it may permit intra-VPC traffic that was never explicitly authorised.
